h1: New noises from a hot-water cylinder
title: New noises from a hot-water cylinder | G3 Cylinder Help
description: Understand new noises from a hot-water cylinder. Distinguish the symptom, gather useful details and arrange competent cylinder assessment in London.
answer: A new noise should be described by timing and location. Heating noise, water movement and pipe vibration can have different causes.

sections.heading: What this symptom can mean
paragraphs: A hum, bang or rush of water is not a universal fault code. Note whether it occurs during heating, at tap closure or with a particular valve or pump. Changes in the connected system can affect the sound.

sections.heading: Information to gather safely
paragraphs: If noise accompanies hot discharge, overheating or an active leak, use the urgent guidance. Otherwise provide a short recording made safely without opening covers or touching hot fittings.

sections.heading: How the enquiry becomes an investigation
paragraphs: The cylinder make, full model and heating arrangement should be identified first. The same visible symptom can arise from different causes, and a relief device may be protecting the system rather than creating the original problem. Component testing and any repair belong to a person competent for the work.

sections.heading: Discuss the appropriate next step
paragraphs: Call 020 7205 4433 with the postcode, symptom history and any previous service findings. The enquiry establishes the proposed assessment and availability. Do not use this guide as a substitute for the actual appliance safety instructions or an on-site diagnosis.

faqs.question: Does a noisy cylinder automatically need descaling?
faqs.answer: No. Noise can originate from different components or water movement; the location, timing and system condition determine the appropriate investigation.
